Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - JXPath154Test.testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM calls doTest("b:foo/test", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "/b:foo[1]/test[1]").
  - doTest builds a JXPathContext over InnerEmptyNamespace.xml and asserts that context.getPointer("b:foo/test").asPath() equals "/b:foo[1]/test[1]".
  - The XML (per the issue description) is of the form:
    - <b:foo xmlns:b="bla" xmlns="test111"> … <test xmlns=""></test> … </b:foo>
    - The inner element <test xmlns=""> resets the default namespace to “no namespace”.

- Where the loop happens:
  - NodePointer.asPath() constructs a path by first delegating to the parent and then appending this node’s segment.
  - Critically, it has a special-case:
    - Lines 681–683: if (parent != null && parent.isContainer()) { return parent.asPath(); }
    - This means: when the parent is a “container” pointer, this node does not append its own segment and relies on the container parent’s asPath to do so.
  - Afterwards (when not returning early), it appends the parent path, a slash if needed, the node’s name (via getName()), and an index if applicable.

- Name resolution for DOM nodes is straightforward and not the source of the loop:
  - DOMNodePointer.getName() builds a QName using:
    - getPrefix(node): Node.getPrefix() or parses Node.getNodeName()
    - getLocalName(node): Node.getLocalName() or parses Node.getNodeName()
  - For <test xmlns="">, getPrefix returns null and getLocalName returns "test", producing a QName that will render as "test". This part does not recurse nor depend on asPath.

- Why the endless loop occurs with an inner empty default namespace:
  - The document is wrapped in a document/container model (DocumentContainer), introducing a “container” parent in the pointer chain.
  - For the selected node (the inner <test>), asPath() attempts to build the path by recursing up to the parent pointers:
    - When a parent in this chain is a container, NodePointer.asPath() returns parent.asPath() without appending this node’s segment (per lines 681–683).
  - The corresponding container parent’s asPath implementation (responsible for formatting its contents) delegates back to the contained value pointer’s asPath() to have the child add its own segment.
  - This creates a circular delegation:
    - Child.asPath() sees a container parent and returns parent.asPath()
    - ParentContainer.asPath() defers to Child.asPath() to append the child’s segment
    - They call each other indefinitely.
  - The inner empty default namespace (<test xmlns="">) is the trigger for this specific pointer chain shape under the DOM model; at that node, the container parent expects the child to render its segment, while the child refuses to render when it sees a container parent. This matches the issue report: “Resetting the default namespace causes a serious endless loop when requesting .asPath() on a node.”

- Evidence mapped to code:
  - The early return that enables the loop is in org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.asPath(), lines 681–683.
  - DOMNodePointer.getName() (lines 180–191) confirms the name building is simple and not recursive, so the loop stems from path assembly, not from QName handling.

- Impact on the test:
  - Instead of producing the expected "/b:foo[1]/test[1]", the asPath() call never completes due to the container–child circular delegation at the point where <test xmlns=""> is encountered.
